quote.text: ...but if you think that only which is your own to be your own, and if you think that what is another’s, as it really is, belongs to another, no man will ever compel you, no man will hinder you, you will never blame any man, you will accuse no man, you will do nothing involuntarily (against your will), no man will harm you, you will have no enemy, for you will not suffer any harm.
quote.author: Epicetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Like Epictetus advises, encourage your children to embrace responsibility for their own thoughts and actions; when children understand ownership of their inner world, they grow into independent individuals who stand firm in their values.
    • By accepting that not every external circumstance or possession is within your control, you invite a parent–child relationship based on mutual respect and freedom, reducing conflicts and fostering genuine trust and understanding.
  • Leadership
    • In leadership, recognizing that you control only your own decisions empowers you to act with integrity and steadfastness; this principle frees you from the paralyzing fear of external criticism.
    • Applying this wisdom means fostering a team culture where each member is trusted to own their responsibilities, enabling everyone to act willingly and harmoniously without coercion, thus creating a more resilient and positive environment.
  • Product Management
    • For a product manager, distinguishing between what you can influence—such as product design and team dynamics—and external factors like market fluctuations is key to maintaining a clear focus and balanced perspective.
    • Embrace the idea that you cannot force external success; instead, concentrate on refining what is within your realm of control (your product’s vision, user experience, and team drive), ensuring that your contributions come from genuine, deliberate intent rather than reactive impulse.
